newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast agrees 41 cocoa licences - trade source.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast agrees 41 cocoa licences - trade source.

text.p: Ivory Coast will grant 41 cocoa and coffee export licences for the 1996/97 season and these should be with exporters by Monday, a trade source told Reuters on Friday.

All 31 exporters licenced for 1995/96 will be given licences. Two new applicants have also been given licences. The remaining eight, taking the total to 41, will also be given licences despite opposition by the Caistab marketing board on financial grounds.

Cocoa and coffee exporters and buyers are also waiting for word from the Caistab marketing agency on their rates under the guideline list of farmgate-to-sea transport prices set at the beginning of each season.
"The list of 41 exporters is final but there are still some points to be talked about on rates," said the source.

The rates are needed to allow the cocoa marketing season, which opened on October 24, to get fully underway after delays to shipments and withdrawals this week of finance by banks in advance of the issuing of licences.
"The discussion will probably go on over the weekend. Exporters should be sent details by Monday," said the source.
The source said exporters' opposition to new tax laws making them responsible for paying buyers income tax at source now centred around how the law would be implemented.
"The law is already in place so we have to apply it. The question is how it can be implemented without creating a dual market of taxed and non-taxed produce."

Under the law, approved by the Ivorian government this year, exporters would pay an amount to the government out of commission exporters pay to buyers for collecting cocoa. They would then have to claim the sum back from the buyer.
Some exporters expect buyers to avoid the tax, about 2.5 CFA per bagged kilo of cocoa, by setting up as tax-exempt cooperatives called GVCs.

Ivory Coast's 1996/97 coffee marketing season was set in September to open at the end of December or at the beginning of January. Coffee is marketed after cocoa from January onwards and so industry attention was this week focused on government announcements on cocoa, which is marketed from October.
Exporters were unavailable for comment on Friday night as most had left work for the weekend.
